votes.reason: At 22.9x trailing earnings that are still 26.1% below the prior four quarters and, per the draft, being guided higher, UNH is priced on the low-point profits of a dominant, low-volatility (2.74% weekly) insurer, so the value case holds despite its 20.74% run over 12 weeks.
At 15.7x trailing with EPS up 13.4% and the sheet's lowest weekly volatility (2.12%), JPM is the cheapest and soundest business in the book, and it has already reported.

A refiner at 22.1x trailing earnings that just jumped 159.9% on war-widened fuel margins, at a 52-week high after a 31.91% run over 12 weeks and with the sheet's highest weekly volatility (5.04%), is priced on peak-cycle profits with the war premium already in the price, so there is no margin of safety if a ceasefire headline narrows those margins.

At 43.2x trailing earnings that shrank 0.9%, a cyclical machinery maker is priced like a growth stock with no growth, the richest non-REIT multiple on the sheet, so even after the pullback a 20% position has no margin of safety if that multiple compresses.

GAAP P/E is the wrong yardstick for a REIT, so the 43.8x multiple and 15.9% EPS drop matter less than the FFO basis the draft cites (15.4x with a ~4% yield), and on that basis this sound landlord, with 3.18% weekly volatility and no report until Aug 10, is still cheap.
